Time: 3 min. Teaching intent: Retrieve prior knowledge before revealing the method.
Talk track: Is 'better performance' a usable objective?
Expected answer / misconception: No. Specify metric, condition, and acceptance rule.
Visual: The three conditions identify what must be compared.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Teach the mechanism or design rule.
Talk track: A package design question needs a workload, interface, operating range, and decision criterion. Trace the visual in order: workload; package requirement; decision. Connect this mechanism to the worked example: Synthetic two-chiplet brief: state power per die, link count, ambient, and maximum allowed temperature as classroom assumptions.
Expected answer / misconception: Ask students to explain the link between adjacent elements; a conceptual diagram is not a measurement.
Visual: Native diagram encodes the causal or design relationship.
[Sources]
R2: IEEE EPS HIR 2024, Ch. 13: Co-Design | https://eps.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/HIR_2024_ch13_HIR_Co-Design.pdf
R6: NIST, Credibility Consideration for Digital Twins | https://www.nist.gov/publications/credibility-consideration-digital-twins-manufacturing

Time: 4 min. Teaching intent: Work the example step by step.
Talk track: Set up the case: Synthetic two-chiplet brief: state power per die, link count, ambient, and maximum allowed temperature as classroom assumptions. Identify the starting information, state the reasoning step aloud, then ask what observation would check the conclusion. Stop before the next slide's question is answered.
Expected answer / misconception: Students must identify the input, the inference, and the check. 
Visual: Three-part reasoning path separates the example from its verification.
